title: A Tumor That Reaches Nerves Without Touching

scenes.tts: A mouse tumor is grafted into a three-day-old chick embryo. The embryo's own nerve fibers invade it. Sympathetic ganglia grow to about six times the size of the same ganglia in control embryos. A ganglion is a cluster of nerve cells outside the brain and spinal cord. Why do they swell?
scenes.visual: Tumor graft inside a chick embryo; fibers reach it; one ganglion beside a control ganglion, a size bar of about six times; a question mark.
scenes.narration: A mouse tumor is grafted into a three-day-old chick embryo. The embryo's own nerve fibers invade it. Sympathetic ganglia grow to about six times the size of the same ganglia in control embryos. A ganglion is a cluster of nerve cells outside the brain and spinal cord. Why do they swell?

scenes.tts: Start with the simplest explanation, contact. The tumor sits inside the embryo, pressed against its tissues. Bueker read his own result as the tumor offering a favorable field for fibers to grow into. So ask one question. Does the tumor need to touch the embryo?
scenes.visual: The tumor touches the tissue, the touch is highlighted, then the question box 'Does it need to touch?' appears.

scenes.tts: So Levi-Montalcini and Hamburger moved the tumor out. The chorio-allantoic membrane is a thin sheet that lines the inside of the eggshell. It is plumbed into the embryo's blood circulation. It touches none of the embryo's internal tissue. They grafted the tumor there.
scenes.visual: Eggshell and membrane drawn around the embryo; the tumor slides out from the embryo onto the membrane; a gap shows no contact; blood vessels link membrane and embryo. Their names appear as the tumor moves out.

scenes.tts: The ganglia deep inside the embryo swelled just as before. Only blood connected the two tissues. So the tumor had to be putting something soluble into it. Contact is ruled out. A substance that travels is ruled in. The graft showed that a molecule must exist, but not what it was.
scenes.visual: Ganglion swells; a tick on 'travels through blood', a cross on 'contact'; closing lists.
